div.head: Rect 6
div.ab: [6] Gafolswane. Gafolswane gebyreð, þæt he sylle his slyht, be ðam ðe on lande stent.
Gafolsƿane (id est ad censum porcario) pertinet, ut suam occisionem det, secundum quod in patria statutum est.
GAFOL SwaNE . Gafolswane gebyreð þæt he sylle his slyht be ðam ðe on lande stent.
Gafolswane Gafolswane gebyreð þæt he sylle his slyht, be ðam ðe on lande stent.
Zins[bäuerlicher] Schweinehirt. Dem zins[bäuerlichen] Schweinehirten kommt zu, dass er sein Schlachtvieh liefere nach dem [Verhältniss], das auf dem Landgute gilt.

The rent-paying swineherd. It is due from the rent-paying swineherd [the personally free tenant of the lord's herd, as opposed to 7] that he deliver his slaughter-pigs according to [the proportion] that holds on the estate.
Tenant swineherd It befits the tenant swineherd that he give his animals for slaughter according to [the custom] that stands on the estate.
Tenant Swineherd It is appropriate that the tenant swineherd give his animals for slaughter, according to the practices observed on the estate.
div.note: Leo and Schmid translate the heading as ‘Be gafolswane’ following 7; but the rubricator repeats only the first word of the chapter; perhaps it served him, already Middle English, as a nominative too (compare ‘fife’ II Cn 30.3a). Liebermann compares Rect 2.; I: first page of the clause in Liebermann, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I, October 2026 (e.g. was “449”, now “448”; 2 rows of Rect)

note.seg: Be ga. übersetzen Leo, Schmid gemäss 7, doch wiederholt Rubricator nur das erste Capitelwort; vielleicht diente es ihm, schon Mittelenglisch, auch als Nom.; vgl. fife II Cnut 30, 3a

Leo and Schmid translate Be ga. in accordance with 7, but the rubricator repeats only the first word of the chapter; perhaps, writing already in Middle English, he also used it as a nom.; cf. fife II Cnut 30, 3a
Persönlich freier Pächter der Herrschaftsherde im Gegensatz zu 7
Personally free tenant of the lord's herd, in contrast to 7

In dem Worte liegt nicht, dass er der Hirt des Viehs der gafolgyldan (der Bauerschaft) sei; ein messarius villatae kommt neben dem herrschaftlichen anderwärts vor; Vinogradoff Villain. 356. Vielmehr die Domänenherde verwaltet er, ebenso wie der Leibeigene in 7. Er ist, im Ggs. zu 6, 4. 7, persönlich frei. Daneben kann er Dorfhirt sein; s. Gl Schwein 7—d

The word does not imply that he is the herdsman of the livestock of the gafolgyldan (the peasantry); a messarius villatae occurs elsewhere alongside the lord's; Vinogradoff Villain. 356. Rather, he manages the demesne herd, just as the serf does in 7. In contrast to 6, 4. 7, he is personally free. He may at the same time be the village herdsman; see Gl Schwein 7—d
‘To be killed’ Toller, Sweet; zwar liefert er nach 6, 1 die Schweine lebendig, richtet aber nach 6, 2 das Fleisch her, also mag slieht ‘Geschlachtetes’ wie sonst bedeuten
‘To be killed’ Toller, Sweet; it is true that according to 6, 1 he delivers the pigs alive, but according to 6, 2 he dresses the meat, so slieht may mean ‘what has been slaughtered’, as elsewhere
